newsitem.title: AFGHANISTAN: Taleban says its forces take strategic Afghan pass.
newsitem.headline: Taleban says its forces take strategic Afghan pass.

text.p: Afghanistan's Taleban movement government said its forces had captured a strategic pass northwest of Kabul on Monday and were moving towards the neighbouring opposition-held province of Baghlan.
The official Voice of Shariat radio said the Taleban seized the Shibber Pass, regarded as a gateway to northern and central Afghanistan, from opposition forces after heavy fighting.

"The Taleban forces, who are in high morale, are chasing the fleeing (opposition) militia and are advancing to Baghlan and God-willing to other northern provinces," the broadcast, monitored in the Pakistani capital Islamabad, said.
Earlier, a Taleban spokesman in Kabul said the Taleban had recaptured a number of positions from the opposition alliance in central Afghanistan.

Taleban information minister Amir Khan Mutaqi said the fighting took place in Lolenj district in the Ghorband valley about 130 km (80 miles), northwest of Kabul. The Ghorband valley leads up to the Shibber Pass.

"Yesterday they launched an attack in Lolenj district and captured some positions. The Islamic army (the Taleban) launched an operation early this morning and retook the captured territory." Mutaqi said. Some weapons and ammunition were recaptured.
There was no independent confirmation of the report.
Mutaqi denied Iranian Radio reports of opposition gains in the eastern Afghan province of Kunar and said the oppositon forces had been defeated and Kunar was under Taleban control.
The Iranian radio report, broadcast on Sunday night, said that anti-Taleban forces had surrounded the provincial capital Assadabad, south of Asmar.
Mutaqi said the Taleban forces had also shot down an opposition plane on the front line in the remote northwestern province of Badghis.
The Taleban are fighting an opposition alliance comprised of forces of the ousted government, northern leader General Abdul Rashid Dostum and Shi'ite Moslem leader Karim Khalili.

An Afghan news service, the Pakistan-based Afghan Islamic Press (AIP), meanwhile, said forces loyal to former government commander Ahmad Shah Masood, Dostum and some Shi'ite Moslem commanders had attacked positions held by former prime minister Gulbuddin Hekmatyar's Hezb-i-Islami party around Baghlan town.

It said the anti-Hekmatyar forces had seized nine military positions from Hezb commander Sayed Rahman in an assault launched on Sunday night. Rahman counter-attacked on Monday, recapturing five of the posts, AIP said.
It said at least four fighters were killed and nine wounded in the fighting but there was no breakdown on how much it had cost each side. Heavy fighting continued in the Baghlan area..
Masood, whose followers are mainly ethnic Tajiks, is an old rival of Hekmatyar and his mainly Pashtun Hezb-i-Islami.

Baghlan, nearly 200 km (125 miles) north of Kabul, is the capital of Baghlan province, one of about nine northern provinces in opposition hands. The Taleban, who captured Kabul in September, control the rest of the country.
